guard: a lifecycle hook retries only missing/refused pre-connect listener errors inside the existing deadline, forwards once after bind, and fails open immediately on permanent local faults
why: A live 0.33.5 manager spawn completed its model turn and nonce DM, but wrote no event WAL.
Instrumenting the shipped MCP handler showed UserPromptSubmit, tool, and terminal frames while
SessionStart never arrived. Claude launched that one-shot hook before the MCP process bound its
local IPC endpoint; runHookRelay treated the first missing-listener error as a final no-op and
discarded the only frame carrying source: startup.
The smoke runs the real relay in a child process and observes its first actual failed dial before
binding a production-shaped Unix socket or Windows named pipe. It also pins the two-second absent
budget and a POSIX ENOTDIR permanent fault, which must fail open immediately rather than making
every lifecycle hook spend the whole retry window on an error no connector startup can repair.

mutations.name: R1 restore the one-shot startup loss on the first missing socket
mutations.expectRed: startup race: relay forwards SessionStart once the connector binds

mutations.name: R2 retry every pre-connect error, stalling hooks on permanent local faults
mutations.expectRed: permanent socket error: fail open immediately instead of retrying for two seconds
mutations.note: On POSIX the smoke connects below a regular file and gets ENOTDIR. The live startup errors ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED remain retryable.
